Introduction

Thank you for giving this a place on your chart.

Helmsman was built for one kind of person: the trader who still makes the decision themselves. Not a signal service, not a black box — a steady pair of hands for the part of the job that is arithmetic and discipline, so the part that needs judgement gets your whole attention.

It is free. Not free-for-now, not free-until-you-need-the-good-features: free, with no activation, no account limit, and nothing locked away. Version 1 does everything you can see in this guide, and it will keep doing it.

That is also the honest part of the deal. Helmsman is the first piece of something larger — a small suite of tools built around manual trading, each one earning its place the same way. Building that takes time, and it takes something from you that costs nothing but matters enormously: a fair rating, and a review or comment that tells me what to fix or what to build next. Every serious suggestion received so far is already in the product. Tell me what is missing, and it goes into the next version.

If something breaks, please say so plainly — a screenshot and the broker name is usually enough. A reproducible report becomes a fix with a proof behind it.

— The developer

Getting started

Install and first attach

Where the file goes

  1. In the terminal, open File → Open Data Folder.
  2. MT5 Copy Helmsman.ex5 into MQL5\Experts.  MT4 Copy Helmsman.ex4 into MQL4\Experts.
  3. Back in the terminal, press Ctrl+M to refresh the Navigator, or simply restart it.
  4. Drag Helmsman from the Navigator onto any chart.
  5. In the dialog that opens, allow algorithmic trading and press OK. Make sure the terminal's own Algo Trading (MT5) or AutoTrading (MT4) button is switched on — with it off the platform refuses every order, and the panel will say so out loud rather than look broken.
Good to know

The values you set in that dialog are first-attach defaults only. From then on the panel itself is the living configuration: whatever you change on screen — position, size, theme, every field — is remembered and restored next time.

One panel per chart

Helmsman manages the symbol of the chart it sits on. Put it on a second chart for a second symbol; each keeps its own settings. If you run two panels at once, give them different Expert ID values so each one manages only its own trades.

MetaTrader 4 or MetaTrader 5?

The same product, built from the same source, on both platforms. Where a platform genuinely cannot do something, this guide marks it with a chip like MT4 and says plainly what happens instead. You will not find a control here that quietly does nothing.

Orientation

The dashboard, part by part

The rail, on the left edge

Four icon tabs — Trade, Manage, Parts, Settings. The blue spine marks where you are.

The header

Stealth appears when hidden levels are available; Stats opens the big window on its charts; News opens that same window on the news tab; and – minimises the panel to its title bar.

The footer strip

The symbol switcher (< XAUUSD >) moves the chart to the next symbol in Market Watch. Beside it sits a clock that turns red when this market is closed, and the time left on the current candle. Small chips appear here when break-even, trailing or partial closes are armed, so you always know what is watching your trade.

Moving and resizing

Drag the title bar to move the panel. Drag the notches in the bottom-right corner to resize the whole thing — the size is remembered along with everything else.

Page one

Trade — from an idea to an order

Everything needed to place one correct trade, in the order a trader actually thinks: direction, then size, then where it fails and where it wins, then what it costs.

SELL and BUY

The two big buttons carry the live bid and ask, so you are never trading against a stale price. With confirmation on (the default) a small dialog shows the entire order before it goes anywhere.

Lot, balance, the money at risk and what percentage of the account that is, the margin it will take, and the three prices. Tick Don't ask again to switch to one-click trading; you can switch it back on the Settings page at any time.

Why this is on by default

One-click trading is faster and, on a bad day, faster in the wrong direction. The dialog costs you a quarter of a second and has prevented more mis-clicks than any feature in this panel.

Plan a trade on the chart

The wide button under the two big ones draws the planning box on the chart. It is explained in full in the next section.

ORDER TYPE

Mkt sends at the market. Stop and Limit place a pending order at the distance in the box beside them, measured in points from the current price. When Stop or Limit is selected, the big buttons rename themselves — BUY STOP +200p — so what you are about to place is never a guess.

RISK > LOT SIZE

This is the heart of the panel. Set how much you are willing to lose, and the lot is calculated for you from the stop distance and the contract of the symbol.

  • The risk stepper — click − or +, or click the number in the middle and type it.
  • The mode box — what that number means: a percentage of Balance, a straight Cash amount in your account currency, a percentage of Equity, or a percentage of Free margin.
  • The Lot field — you can also work the other way round. Type a lot size and the risk figure re-computes itself to match. Neither number is ever a leftover from the other.

STOP · TARGET · RATIO

The stop and target distances in points, and the reward-to-risk ratio between them. Type in any of the three and the others follow: change the stop and the target moves to hold the ratio; type a target and the ratio re-computes. Press the RR button to unlink them when you want the target somewhere structural instead.

The money card

Four lines that turn the plan into money, recalculated on every tick:

LineWhat it tells you
Risk The money that is actually at stake and what share of the balance it is. Green up to your comfortable limit, amber up to the danger limit, red beyond it. If no valid lot exists, this line says so and the note underneath explains exactly why — usually that the risk is too small for the broker's minimum lot.
Costs The spread right now in points and in money, plus commission per lot. Leave the commission input at zero and the panel estimates it from your own closed trades, marking the figure (auto est.) so you know where it came from.
Margin What this trade will take, and what stays free afterwards.
Reward The money at the target, and the distance in points.

Quick actions — on the trades you already have

  • Breakeven — move the stop of every open position to its own entry price.
  • Close % — close that percentage of every position; the percentage sits in the box beside the button.
  • OCO — a bracket: a buy stop above the market and a sell stop below it. When one fills, the other is cancelled automatically. If a fast market fills both, the later one is closed and the panel tells you it did.

Close positions & delete pending

The coloured buttons carry live totals, so you always know what you are about to close: Buys, ALL, Sells, and then Profit (every position currently in profit) and Loss. Underneath, All / Limits / Stops delete pending orders by family.

Stealth mode

With Stealth lit, your stop, target and pending orders stop being broker-side orders and become panel-side levels. The broker sees a naked position; Helmsman watches the price and executes the level itself.

Understand this one before using it

A hidden level only exists while the panel is running. Close the terminal, lose the connection, or remove the expert and the level goes with it — the position stays open and unprotected. The panel states this on screen whenever stealth is armed.

In this screenshot you can also see the close buttons carrying their live totals, and the money card explaining, in words, why no lot can be produced at that risk.

On the chart

Planning a trade with your hands

Press Plan a trade on the chart and three lines appear — entry, stop and target — with a shaded box between them. The button changes to Planning — drag the box, OK sends it so you know the panel is waiting for you.

Grab any line anywhere along its length; there is no need to select it first. Drag the entry line and the whole box moves with it. Every number on the panel updates while you drag.

The OK tag knows what you drew

Drag the entry above the market and the tag becomes OK · BUY STOP; below it, OK · BUY LIMIT; at the market, OK · BUY. Click it and that order is sent, with the stop and target exactly where the lines are.

Right-click a line

  • Place the order now — same as pressing OK.
  • Trailing stop: next rule — step through the trailing rules; the stop tag immediately shows the chosen rule by name, so you can see that it took.
  • Trailing stop: off.
  • Remove the box.
  • Nothing — close this menu.

Everywhere else on the chart, your platform's own right-click menu is untouched. Helmsman only takes it over its own lines and its own panel.

What the labels can show

Every line label is built from tokens you choose on the Settings page: the kind of level, the lot size, the distance in points, the money, that money as a percentage of balance, the reward-to-risk ratio, and the price. Turn off what you do not read; the chart restyles instantly.

Page two

Manage — what happens after you are in

The rules that watch the trade for you. Everything here applies to positions you open from now on and, with one button, to everything already open.

The headline and the list

The top line counts your open positions, their total lots and their live profit. Under it, each position gets a row with its direction, size, entry and money. Click a row and that single trade opens in its own window.

AUTO-PROTECT (break-even + trailing)

Arm at profit is how far into profit the trade must go before the stop is moved. Lock offset is how far beyond the entry the stop lands — a few points past break-even so the spread cannot take you out at exactly zero.

The box below picks the trailing rule by name, and the field beside it is that rule's one number. Apply to open positions stamps both onto every trade you already have.

The trailing rules, in plain words

RuleWhat it doesThe number beside it
OffNo trailing.—
Fixed distance The stop follows price at a constant distance. points
ATR distance The distance breathes with volatility, measured by ATR on a timeframe you choose. × ATR
Follow MA line The stop tracks a moving average, kept a small indent away. indent, points
Follow PSAR The stop tracks the parabolic SAR dots. step / max
Last fractal The stop sits beyond the most recent fractal high or low. indent, points
N-bar high/low The stop sits beyond the extreme of the last N candles. bars
Keep % profit Whatever the best profit reached, keep this share of it locked. percent
Step by timer The stop tightens by a fixed step every so many seconds — for trades you want out of on a clock. points / seconds

CLOSE EVERYTHING WHEN

Two account-level exits: close every position when the net result reaches a profit, or when it reaches a loss. Switch either on and it arms itself as soon as you edit the amount. The third toggle also deletes pending orders when it fires, so a triggered basket does not leave orders behind.

PENDING ORDERS · BASKET

  • Trail pendings at — pending orders follow the price at the given distance until they fill, so a breakeout order keeps its distance from a market that walked away.
  • Basket break-even line on chart — draws one dashed line at the single price where all your open positions together break even. For anyone averaging into a position, this is the number that matters.

Grid…

Opens the grid window: levels, spacing (fixed points or from ATR), lot multiplier, base lot, and whether the grid builds behind price with limit orders or ahead of it with stop orders. One real order is placed per level. Drag the first grid line on the chart and every other level re-spaces itself around it.

PANIC — flat everything

One button that closes every position and deletes every pending order on this symbol. It arms on the first click and turns red; a second click within five seconds fires it. Wait longer and it disarms itself.

The line under the card always tells you what is armed and what the news module currently knows, so the Manage page is readable at a glance without opening anything.

Page three

Parts — taking money off in pieces

A ladder of partial closes. The left column is your profit steps, the right column your loss steps, ten of each. Every row has three controls: a switch to arm it, how much of the trade to close, and how far away that happens.

The row at the top of the page reads exactly like a sentence: row 1 = close 50% at +300pt profit.

What the numbers mean — the unit picker

  • Levels in points — a plain distance from entry.
  • Levels in % — a percentage of this trade's own target distance (and of its own stop distance on the loss side). Set 50% and every trade banks its first piece halfway to its target, whatever the symbol.
  • Levels in R — multiples of the risk you took, where 1R is your stop distance.

How much to close

% of initial measures against the size you opened with; % of current measures against whatever is left.

Apply to open stamps the ladder onto every position you already have. Levels also apply automatically to new trades.

Two details that save real money

Every armed level is drawn on the chart at its real price with its own tag, and a level that has fired greys out and is labelled done instead of vanishing — so you can see both what happened and what is still waiting. And if closing a piece would leave less than the broker's minimum lot behind, the panel closes the whole remainder instead of leaving an unclosable crumb.

If a level refuses

A broker can refuse a partial close — bad price, a busy trade context, a volume it will not accept. Helmsman tries three times, then disarms that level for that position and writes the broker's own reason on this page. It will not sit there retrying and beeping at you forever.

Page four

Settings — the panel itself

Show on chart labels

Seven switches decide what every line label on the chart contains: Kind (SL, TP, BUY STOP…), Lots, Points, Money, % Balance, RR and Price. Every line restyles the moment you flip one.

One-click

Off by default: every order shows its confirmation dialog first. Turn it on when you want orders to go straight out.

Hotkeys

Arms the keyboard chords listed in their own section.

Panel scale

A manual zoom for the whole dashboard. Leave it and the panel follows your screen's DPI; set 1.25 or 1.50 on a very large monitor.

Screenshot now · Save preset · Load preset

A one-click chart screenshot into the terminal's files folder, and your whole panel configuration saved to — or restored from — a preset file.

Theme

Dark, Light, Midnight blue and Slate & amber. Every surface, including the floating windows and the chart labels, restyles live.

The four themes

About / account info

Opens the page below: who your broker is, the account number, whether it is hedging or netting, the leverage and the currency — then the facts of the symbol you are trading, including how many points make one pip on this symbol. That single line explains why a distance that felt right at one broker feels ten times tighter at another.

Journal / stats

A short summary of your closed trades, with a line that checks the panel's own arithmetic against the broker's history and says verified when they agree to the cent.

Show The 60-Second Tour Again

The welcome card that names every control appears once, on your first attach, and a click anywhere on it puts it away for good. If you sent it away in your first ten seconds and wished you had not, this brings it back — as often as you like.

Rules And Protection

Six pages of guard rails: the Guardian, trading hours, alerts, the four-stage break-even, the news guard, and what to do about trades you did not open here. Each is explained in its own section later on.

Redraw The Panel

The whole dashboard is a single object drawn onto your chart. Loading a chart template, or any tool that clears chart objects, can take it away — and until now the only way back was to remove the panel and add it again. Helmsman notices within a quarter of a second and rebuilds itself, but if you have just watched it vanish you should not have to take that on trust. This button rebuilds it on the spot, and it is harmless to press when nothing is wrong.

Confirm Bulk Close And Delete

On by default. The buttons that close a group of trades or delete your waiting orders ask for a second click first, and they say exactly what they are about to do — Click Again Within Five Seconds To Close 3 Positions. Neither act can be undone, and a mouse can slip. Switch it off if you want the single click back.

Keyboard shortcuts are not affected. Shift+C and the rest act at once, because a two-key chord is already something you did on purpose.

Floating window

One position, on its own

Click any row in the Manage list and that trade opens here, titled with its ticket, direction and size.

Lock Stop and Lock Target are the two switches under the price boxes. With one on, that line still sits on the chart with its handle, but dragging it does nothing to your trade: the line glides back to where the broker has it and the panel says Stop Is Locked. Typing a price in the box above still works — the lock guards the gesture, not the decision. It lasts for the session.

  • The headline — live profit in your account currency, green or red.
  • The graph — this trade's own profit since the window opened. The dotted line is break-even, so you can see at a glance whether it has ever been in the money.
  • SL and TP — type a price and press Apply SL / TP; it goes straight to the broker.
  • Close, Close 50%, Reverse (close and open the same size the other way), Breakeven now.
  • The trailing box and “This one” — a trailing rule for this position only. The rest of your book keeps its own rules.

The window closes itself when the position is gone, so it can never describe something that no longer exists.

Floating window

Stats, news and closed trades

One window, three tabs, opened from Stats or News in the header. Drag it by the title, resize it from the corner, close it with the red X — and it places itself where the recent candles are not.

Charts

News

Trades

ColumnMeaning
ClosedWhen the trade ended.
TradeDirection and size.
HeldHow long the position was open.
Open / CloseThe two prices.
Pips The move in pips for this broker — ten points make a pip on a 3- or 5-digit quote, one point on a 2- or 4-digit one.
GrossThe price result, before costs.
CommCommission charged on the trade.
SwapOvernight financing paid or received.
NetWhat actually reached your balance.

Click any row and it expands: the ticket, when it opened, how long it was held, the move in pips and points with this symbol's points-per-pip spelled out, the full cost breakdown, and the result in R.

About the spread column

There is not one, and that is deliberate. Brokers do not record a per-trade spread anywhere in the history — its cost is already inside Gross. Rather than print a number that looks precise and is not, the table says so at the bottom.

Protection

Guardian — the rules that stop you

Every guard is off by default. Switch on only what you want, from Settings › Rules And Protection › Guardian — or from the inputs before you attach, if you prefer to set a chart up once and forget it. When one fires it says which rule and until when — and closing trades always stays allowed, even while entries are locked.

GuardWhat it watchesWhat happens
Daily loss Balance against the day's starting point. Locks new entries for the rest of the trading day, and optionally flattens what is open.
Max drawdown Equity against its own highest point. Same lock, measured from the peak instead of the day.
Trades per day How many entries you have taken today. Refuses further entries once the cap is reached.
Consecutive losses Losing trades in a row. A cooling-off brake for the minutes you set; the panel names the time it expires.
Friday flat The clock on Friday. Closes everything at the time you choose and locks the weekend.
Spread gate The spread at the moment you press buy or sell. Blocks the entry and shows both numbers — the spread now and the limit you set.
Equity target Account equity rising to an amount. Banks the day: flattens everything once and locks.
Equity floor Account equity falling to an amount. Flattens everything once and locks.
Trading window Server time and the weekday. Entries only inside your hours and on your chosen days; an optional daily flatten at a set time.

Guard state survives a restart, so a lock cannot be escaped by closing the terminal and opening it again.

Protection

Rules And Protection — six pages of guard rails

Six things used to be reachable only through the properties dialog before the panel opened: the Guardian, your trading hours, alerts, the four-stage break-even, the news guard, and what happens to trades you did not open here. They now live behind one door on the Settings page, and every edit takes effect the moment you make it — there is no Apply button to forget.

Settings › Rules And Protection opens the list. Nothing on any of these pages is on until you switch it on, and none of them can stop you closing a trade. They only ever stand between you and opening one.

Guardian — account limits

The fourteen controls that decide when Helmsman stops letting you open trades: the daily loss limit and the hour your day re-anchors, the drawdown limit measured from your equity's own peak, a cap on trades per day, a timed brake after losing trades in a row, the Friday flatten, a spread gate, and an equity target and floor.

Trading hours and weekdays

A window entries are allowed inside, and a row of seven switches for the days. Set the closing time earlier than the opening time for a window that runs through midnight. Below it, a daily flatten with its own time, and whether it removes waiting orders too.

Alerts

Which events speak — fills, closes, waiting orders — and through which channel: the terminal's sound, its popup, a push to your phone, or email. Push needs your MetaQuotes ID set in the terminal and email needs its mail settings; the panel does not pretend otherwise. The last switch saves a chart image on every fill and close, linked from the journal.

Multi-level break-even

Four stages instead of one jump. Each stage has a profit that arms it and a place the stop goes, in points beyond entry. This is separate from the single break-even on the Manage page, and it applies to new trades.

News guard

How long before a calendar event entries stop, how long after they stay stopped, and whether everything is closed ahead of it. The impact filter decides which events count at all.

Outside trades

What Helmsman does about a position it did not open — one you placed by hand, from your phone, or that another robot opened. Ignore it, announce it, or protect it automatically. The stop, target and risk used for that protection are the Trade page's own current numbers; adoption borrows them rather than keeping a second set you would have to remember to update.

Four settings deliberately stay in the properties dialog: the two sound filenames, the news file path and the news feed address. They are text, and the panel cannot yet remember text you type across a restart — a box that quietly forgets what you put in it is worse than no box. They will move here when it can.

News — and where it comes from

With the news guard on, Helmsman refuses new entries from a few minutes before a filtered event until a few minutes after it, and can optionally flatten once before impact. The refusal always names the event.

MetaTrader 5

MT5 Nothing to set up. The terminal has a built-in economic calendar and the panel reads it directly.

MetaTrader 4 — pick one of two

MT4 MetaTrader 4 has no calendar at all, so Helmsman brings its own. Both routes are honest about where the data came from, and the news tab always prints the source.

Option 1 — straight from the internet (simplest)

  1. In the terminal, open Tools → Options → Expert Advisors.
  2. Tick Allow WebRequest for listed URL.
  3. Add this address to the list, exactly as written:
    https://nfs.faireconomy.media
  4. Press OK, then set the panel's input Fetch the calendar over the internet to true.

The feed is the weekly ForexFactory calendar in JSON — the same one MT4 news tools have used for years. If you ever want a different provider, the address is an input; anything serving the same fields works.

If you skip the whitelist

The panel does not show an empty list and leave you guessing. It prints the exact sentence: which URL to allow, and the menu it lives in. That is your switch to flip — no product can flip it for you.

Option 2 — from a file, with no internet permission

If you also run MetaTrader 5 on the same computer, attach the small companion expert HelmNewsExport to any MT5 chart. It writes the terminal's own calendar into the folder both platforms share, and every MT4 running Helmsman reads it from there. No web permission, and the data is MetaQuotes' own.

You can also point the input Custom news CSV at any file you maintain yourself. One event per line:

epoch,currency,importance(1-3),title,previous,forecast

News guard

Straight talk

What Helmsman will not do

  • It will not tell you what to trade. There are no signals here and none are planned. The decision stays yours.
  • It will not pretend a number it cannot know. Where a figure is estimated it is labelled; where a broker records nothing, the panel says so instead of inventing a value.
  • It will not fail silently. Every refusal — from the broker, from a guard, from the risk maths — is spoken in plain words, with the reason.
  • It will not hide behind a paywall later. Free, without activation or an account ceiling.
  • Hidden levels are not magic. Stealth levels live in the panel. If the terminal is closed, they are not watching anything, and the panel tells you that whenever stealth is on.

MT4 Four things the older platform simply cannot do, stated once: it has no economic calendar (use one of the two routes above), no stop-limit orders (asking for one is refused in words), no asynchronous closing (group closes are sequential and report what happened), and no netting accounts — every MetaTrader 4 account hedges.

Help

Support, and reporting a bug

Version 1 is the beginning of this tool, not the end of it. If something is wrong, or missing, or simply awkward — say so, and it gets fixed.

The fastest way to get a fix

  1. A screenshot of the panel or the chart at the moment it happened.
  2. Your broker and account type — the About page on the Settings tab has every fact needed, in one screen.
  3. What you expected, and what happened instead.

That is usually enough to reproduce a problem exactly, and a reproducible problem becomes a fix with a proof behind it.

Where to write

  • Email the developer directly — shaikhsadi049@gmail.com. Bug reports and feature requests are read personally, and a clear one usually gets a reply with a plan.
  • The Comments tab of the product page — best for questions others will have too.
  • A private message to the author on MQL5.com — best for account details or anything you would rather not post publicly.
  • A review — the single most useful thing you can do for this project. A fair rating and one honest sentence about what to build next is what keeps a free tool moving forward.
